messages:
Zach: heads-up — after flipping the NTK-style RoPE scaling for mixtral-8x in the longctx canary, we see a perf regression + quality drift. p95 latency jumped ~22% and eval perplexity on the llama-suite rose ~0.38. PerfBot alerted this morning.
Emma: can you paste the key numbers and where you changed the config? link to the canary?
Zach: canary: canary-us-west-2/mixtral-8x/ntk-rope-2026-03-21. brief snapshot: 
```
model         config              p95(ms)  throughput(tok/s)  ppl(delta)
mixtral-8x    ntk-rope            62       1450               +0.38
mixtral-8x    linear-rope         51       1600               +0.01
qwen-7b       ntk-rope            34       2200               +0.00
llama-2-13b   ntk-rope            78       900                +0.42
```
Zach: stacktrace from one hot path shows kernel selector picking `attn_opt_v2` with headKV layout for several sequences — but the kernel's warp utilization drops on longctx, causing more stalls. KV cache GC runs more often (eviction threshold hit).
PerfBot: [alert] increased tail latency detected for mixtral-8x on NTK-RoPE variants. Evidence: p95 up 22%, retry rate +1.2%.
Raj: interesting — could be interaction between the RoPE frequency remap and headKV stride. Did we change head/kv dims mapping in the quantized build?
Olivia: I touched the kernel routing patch yesterday to prefer attn_opt_v2 for ntk-like offsets. I can revert quickly if we want. Also saw KV slot churn in GPU profiler (see flame graph link).
Emma: before revert, can we validate two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection -> fallback to attn_ref reduces latency and keeps quality, 2) batching heuristic sensitivity (target_latency_ms) amplifies stalls because small batches keep sending odd sequence lengths.
Zach: I ran quick local repro with `TARGET_LAT_MS=8` vs `16`. Results: lower target (8) -> smaller batches -> more kernel switches -> p95 worse. Higher target -> batching masks the stall and p95 improves but throughput drops slightly.
Raj: plan: bisect kernel router decisions for the canary. Steps: (a) run canary with `kernel_forced=attn_ref` for 2h, (b) run with `kernel_forced=attn_opt_v2` but set `batcher.target_latency_ms=16`, (c) run `rope_variant=linear` for comparison. Olivia, can you toggle (a) and (c)? I'll do (b) and collect traces.
Olivia: on it. toggled (a) now. DeployBot: canary update: mixtral-8x kernel_forced=attn_ref by Olivia at 2026-03-21T10:12Z.
PerfBot: canary metrics starting — p95 dropping back to ~49ms on attn_ref, ppl still slightly up (+0.12). Throughput stable.
Zach: ppl improvement suggests kernel path caused numerical jitter with ntk remap on headKV. Might be precision/order differences. We should run small eval set to check generation diffs. Olivia, can you run 500-sample deterministic eval?
Olivia: kicked off eval job `rope-bisect-eval-238001` (500 deterministic samples across mixtral/llama/qwen). ETA ~35m.
Emma: if eval shows quality regression only for mixtral, we can restrict the ntk-rope default per-model safe range. Add config knob: `rope_mode: per_model {mixtral: linear; qwen: ntk}`.
Raj: agree. Also logging action: add a kernel telemetry tag when switching based on RoPE variant so backfills can correlate ppl deltas with kernel choices. I'll own the telemetry PR.
Zach: filing followups: 1) rollback ntk default for mixtral if eval shows >0.2 ppl delta, 2) add per-model rope safe ranges, 3) kernel-router bisect doc. Punting to Monday for full rollout. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Emma: solid. keep thread updated when eval finishes.
PerfBot: [info] eval job rope-bisect-eval-238001 queued.
Olivia: eval finished — summary paste: `mixtral: ppl +0.36 ntk vs linear; llama: +0.41; qwen: +0.02`. Uploading full diffs to S3. link: https://s3.redwood-inf/experiments/238001/diffs.gz
Zach: ok that's actionable. I'll open rollback change and a canary with explicit per-model rope mapping. Closing loop after PR + canary.
Emma: thanks — add a note in the release changelog about kernel selection heuristic tweak and per-model safe ranges.
Raj: PRs: telemetry (#4527), kernel-router-bisect (#4528), rollout-rollback (#4529). I'll tag reviewers.
